title: Hightide Inventory Assistant oncall notes
content:
Context:
- Hightide Logistics (warehouse chain, 24 sites) wants an LLM-driven inventory assistant that runs in their edge PoPs (air-gapped-ish). Pilot = 3 warehouses for 8 weeks.
- Primary UX: operators scan/photograph SKU, assistant returns suggested putaway location + short consolidation advice + short confidence score.
- We're proposing Redwood Private (VPC) in their AWS accounts with a thin edge proxy for local inference via gRPC -> routed back to Private control plane for billing/rollout only.

Call notes (2024-09-17, 11:00 PT)
- Attendees: Diego (RWI), Priya (RWI), Marcus (Hightide infra), Lena (Hightide ops), Sam (Hightide product).
- Marcus: security is top priority. No outbound to public internet except to our control plane endpoints (TLS mutual auth).
- Lena: typical site bandwidth is 50–100 Mbps but high jitter during shift changes. Latency to regional cloud ~45–120ms.
- Sam: target response SLA for operator = 300ms median, 800ms p95 for small payloads (text + single sku image).
- We sketched fallback: local cache + on-device rules if model unavailable.

Requirements captured:
- Networking: Mutual TLS, customer-managed VPC endpoints, allowlist only for control plane IPs. No direct model downloads to site; models remain in customer VPC region.
- KMS: Customer wants HSM-backed keys (AWS CloudHSM) for encryption at rest of prompt history and logs.
- Data residency: logs retained in their account; we must support customer-side logging S3 path + lifecycle policy.
- Throughput target: baseline 30 req/s across 3 warehouses, allow bursts to 90 req/s. Typical request size = ~60 tokens (generation + metadata).
- Model: start with gpt-like 7B distilled variant (quantized) for latency; fallback to 13B for complex cases.
- Failover: if Private region saturated, route to Redwood hosted fallback within same region only if customer permits.

Gotchas / risks (notes to self)
- Tokenization oddities for product SKUs: many contain slashes and dashes; tokenizer splits unpredictably. Need deterministic pre-tokenization step (escape slashes or use raw bytes embedding).
- Image -> multimodal pipeline: current thin-proxy forwards base64 image; but we saw 2x latency hit due to proxy JSON encode. Consider compress + multipart binary gRPC.
- Site jitter impacts KV cache expiry decisions: aggressive caching helps p95 but hurts freshness for near-real-time inventory. Need workload study.
- Edge GPU memory: customer edge servers are A10G-like (24GB). Our 7B quantized pipeline needs careful KV cache memory budgeting at sequence lengths >512.
- Firewall teams sometimes NAT many devices behind single IP; rate-limiting per IP can be problematic. Recommend token-based client id + rate limiter keyed to client id rather than IP.
- Approval chain: Marcus said infra approvals could take 4–6 weeks; schedule accordingly.

Action items / next steps
- Diego: produce a 1-page network diagram + minimal firewall rules and mTLS handshake flow for Marcus by EOD 2024-09-20. (PRIORITY)
- Priya: produce cost estimate for Private + expected token/unit costs at 30/90 req/s thresholds; include quantized model variants. Due 2024-09-25.
- Marcus: confirm CloudHSM availability and provide KMS contact. Due 2024-09-24.
- Lena: provide sample inventory SKU list (CSV) and a few representative photos (phone). Lena to sanitize PII. Due 2024-09-22.
- Diego + Marcus: quick perf check — run small throughput test over their VPN to a staging Private region; validate p95 under jitter. Tentative 2024-09-30.
- All: sync next week Wed 2024-09-24 10:00 PT for status.

Open questions (need answers before design finalization)
- Does Hightide allow any cross-region failover to Redwood hosted endpoints? (Marcus: probably no by default).
- Do we need SCC (segment-level) telemetry exported to Hightide's Splunk? If yes, we must map events and costs.
- Authorization model: will Hightide prefer IAM role mapping per warehouse or a single service principal? impacts key rotation.
- Image pre-processing: should we recommend local image resizing (mobile devices) vs accepting full-res and resizing at proxy? bandwidth tradeoff.

Quick notes / heuristics to test in pilot
- Try prefix caching with a short TTL (10s) for repeated SKU queries during packing bursts. Measure stale-assist rate.
- Use request batching window 5–8ms for throughput improvements but ensure median latency degradation <25ms.
- Tokenize SKUs with custom rule: treat slash (/) as single token to avoid fragmentation. Test across models.

Draft rollback plan (if pilot breaks)
- Step 1: flip to local rule-based assistant (simple lookup; no model calls) for affected warehouse.
- Step 2: throttle model calls (reduce to 5 req/s per warehouse), increase batch window to rebuild throughput.
- Step 3: collect debug traces, escalate to eng-serving-runtime on-call (SE-4872).

Random observations (notes to self)
- Lena is skeptical of any model that "hallucinates" location names — need explicit controlled vocab and classification head, not pure open generation.
- Marcus suggested a separate ingress for telemetry to avoid adding load to inference plane. Good idea.

Short-term deliverables (by next sync)
- Network diagram + firewall rules (Diego)
- Cost estimate + model variant tradeoffs (Priya)
- Sample data + photos (Lena)
- Perf test plan (Diego + Marcus)

Playbook tags for future: pilot-hightide, edge-vpn, sku-tokenization, cloudhsm-integration.
